newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed mixed on Thursday after a noncommittal session spent worrying about Friday's upcoming U.S. August employment figures, which could prove key to U.S. near term interest rate policy.

U.S. jobless claims figures for the week to end-August were stronger than expected, causing the AEX share index to lurch down to its session low on worries tomorrow's figures will show similar strength. The AEX closed 1.08 points down at 553.08.
"People are again scared about interest rates," said a dealer. "The jobless claim figure today shows that strength in the U.S. economy is still there," he added.

Dealers said Wall Street's double-figure swoop lower at the opening had dragged the Dutch market along with it, a measure of nervousness about tomorrow's figures and a sign that the market here is hesitating about domestic fundamentals.

"We've had most of the important Dutch companies' first half reports so there's not much more support to come from there. The dollar's not going anywhere so the market's finding it difficult to come up with a direction," a dealer said."
He said support at 552 on the AEX appeared to be forming. "It's very important to hold this level. If it doesn't it could go down to 540, that's what everyone's talking about."

Technical analysts say the current chart formations equally indicate a climb to above 600 is possible as the market is forming an inverted head and shoulders, the peak of which points to 610 within six months.
The index's all-time high of 572.50 was scored in June.
Dealers detected signs of profit-taking, particularly in Royal Dutch down 1.50 guilders to 255.10 and Unilever 80 cents easier at 248.10 guilders.
Royal Dutch has been rising on fears of oil supply disruption following the recent flare-up between Iraq and the U.S. after Iraqi actions against Kurds in northern Iraq.
"The crude price is a bit weaker and things are not getting out of hand in Iraq so a drift was predictable," a dealer said.
Unilever saw profit-takers nibble back part of a 10.50 guilder gain since its new UK chairman's comments at the weekend about streamlining the company's sprawling business portfolio.

Ahold closed 30 cents higher at 93.30 guilders following second quarter net profit of 121.3 million guilders, up from a previous of 102.5 million and at the top end of analysts' forecasts of 110.7-123.00 million guilders. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
